LLM auditresponse for fix-certs-pyopenssl.patch:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided file is a patch (`fix-certs-pyopenssl.patch`) that modifies a test utility class `Certs` in a Python test file. The change replaces the use of the older `pyOpenSSL` library with the more modern and actively maintained `cryptography` library to generate self-signed TLS certificates for testing purposes.

The patch removes code that used `OpenSSL.crypto` and replaces it with equivalent functionality using `cryptography.hazmat.primitives` and related modules. The new code generates a 4096-bit RSA key pair, constructs a certificate with subject and issuer set to "Dapr" and "localhost", sets validity to one day, optionally adds a Subject Alternative Name (SAN) for "localhost" in HTTP mode, and writes the resulting certificate and private key in PEM format to disk. All operations are confined to test setup and certificate generation for local use.

There are no signs of malicious behavior: no network requests, no data exfiltration, no use of dangerous or obfuscated code. The changes improve security hygiene by moving away from `pyOpenSSL`, which is no longer recommended for new projects, to the well-vetted `cryptography` library. The file operates entirely within the scope of expected test utility functionality.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Patch replaces pyOpenSSL with cryptography for test certificates; no malicious code.</summary>
</security_assessment>
